note: Weekly deep-reading pool. Ordered best first, with eight additions versus last week and a mix of current first-party engineering work and durable foundational papers. The dashboard can rotate through unused items with Different one.

pool.title: The Thin Orchestrator: How We Made Our AI Agents More Reliable by Giving the Router Less to Do
pool.why: How a small deterministic router, isolated specialist contexts, and explicit reliability checks can outperform a monolithic agent architecture.

pool.title: Cutting our inference bill by 68% by being obsessive about optimization
pool.why: How shared prompt caching, fewer redundant model calls, parallel tool work, and model routing jointly reduced the cost and latency of an AI code-review system.

pool.title: Building a data plane from scratch: Stripe’s own high-performance distributed proxy
pool.why: How Stripe replaced Envoy with a purpose-built Go proxy to improve service-mesh efficiency while targeting five-and-a-half nines of reliability.

pool.title: Inside Prometheus: Meta’s Journey to a Gigawatt-Scale Supercluster
pool.why: How power, liquid cooling, Ethernet fabrics, failure handling, and workload goodput fit together in a gigawatt-scale training cluster.

pool.title: Analyzing technical documents with Deep Review
pool.why: How segmentation, adaptive compute budgets, parallel verification, and global synthesis can make agentic review of long technical documents more rigorous.

pool.title: How Stripe uses graph search and state machines to auto-remediate a global database fleet
pool.why: How graph modeling, pathfinding, and state machines can generate safe recovery plans for a changing global database topology.

pool.title: Building agents with the Claude Agent SDK
pool.why: How filesystem-based context gathering, subagents, tool design, and compaction support production agents that run beyond a single prompt.

pool.title: Uber’s Journey to Ray on Kubernetes: Ray Setup
pool.why: How Uber moved distributed ML workloads to Ray on Kubernetes and designed a federated layer to simplify resource requests and improve utilization.

pool.title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
pool.why: How agent-scale development changes version-control requirements, and how Anthropic removed a fast-growing merge bottleneck through a five-month migration to an in-house system.

pool.title: Under the hood, off the hot path: How D1 scales to millions of databases
pool.why: How to separate a database control plane from edge query execution while managing millions of databases on a shared developer platform.

pool.title: Writing effective tools for agents — with agents
pool.why: How evaluation-driven iteration, namespacing, concise tool responses, and clear error feedback make tools easier for agents to discover and use correctly.

pool.title: Open and Emergent Problems in Agentic Privacy and Security: A Contextual Angle
pool.why: Why static permissions break down for probabilistic agents, and how contextual policy engines, sandboxing, user controls, and multi-agent evaluation can form layered defenses.

pool.title: Cloudflare Containers, rebuilt to scale agent sandboxes
pool.why: How runtime-selected images, Durable Object-owned lifecycles, colocated scheduling, and filesystem snapshots make on-demand agent sandboxes faster and recoverable.

pool.title: The Agent Said It Was Done. The Database Disagreed.
pool.why: How to evaluate stateful agents against terminal backend state, side effects, and repeated-run consistency instead of trusting prose or valid-looking tool calls.

pool.title: Towards a science of scaling agent systems: When and why agent systems work
pool.why: How task decomposability, sequential dependencies, and tool density determine whether single-agent, centralized, or parallel architectures will help or amplify errors.

pool.title: An Organizational Second Brain: Building an AI That Learns From Experts
pool.why: How structured knowledge files, composable reasoning recipes, evaluation gates, and expert-feedback compilation create auditable institutional memory without retraining.

pool.title: Harness design for long-running application development
pool.why: How planner, generator, and evaluator agents, structured handoffs, context resets, and skeptical grading make multi-hour coding runs more coherent.

pool.title: ReasoningBank: Enabling agents to learn from experience
pool.why: How to distill successes and failures into reusable reasoning memories, then combine them with parallel and sequential test-time exploration.

pool.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
pool.why: How to manage instructions, tools, history, retrieval, and compaction as a finite attention budget rather than treating context as an unlimited prompt.

pool.title: Scaling Managed Agents: Decoupling the brain from the hands
pool.why: How durable session logs and independently replaceable harnesses and sandboxes turn long-running agents from fragile pets into recoverable services.

pool.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
pool.why: Why KV-cache fragmentation wastes accelerator memory, and how OS-style paging plus continuous batching raises serving throughput without changing model outputs.

pool.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
pool.why: Why attention is memory-bound, and how IO-aware tiling makes exact attention dramatically faster without approximation.

pool.title: Saving another 100TB of RAM with math and Rust
pool.why: How probability, consistent hashing, and careful data-structure work removed more than 100 TB of fleet-wide memory use from a Pingora service.

pool.title: How we built our multi-agent research system
pool.why: How an orchestrator delegates parallel research, manages context, and balances higher token cost against coverage and quality.

pool.title: Spanner: Google's Globally-Distributed Database
pool.why: How TrueTime enables externally consistent transactions across a global database despite clock uncertainty and replication delay.

pool.title: Attention Is All You Need
pool.why: How self-attention, multi-head attention, positional encoding, and encoder-decoder blocks replaced recurrence with a parallelizable sequence architecture.

pool.title: Designing robust and predictable APIs with idempotency
pool.why: How idempotency keys and server-side request semantics make network retries safe without duplicating side effects.
